text:
Leni Park: hey everyone 1 excited to join Growth! i'm Leni (she/they), usually remote from seattle but hoping to be in SF a couple times a month. fun fact: i play ukulele very badly and bake experimental vegan cookies that somehow keep coworkers alive. any recs for where to stash a loaf of cookies so it survives the day? :uke:
WelcomeBot: welcome to Redwood, Leni! :wave: Check the #new-hires guide and you'll get the welcome lunch invite soon.
Omar Z: hi Leni, welcome! we have a "snack shelf" in the kitchenette (third shelf from the top) that's usually safe. pro tip: label with name + date and add a warning like "vegan cookie, do not microwave" to prevent curiosity nukes. :cookie:
Talia H: welcome!! if you're ever baking extras, drop them off near the coffee station after 10am 1 people swarm less then. and bonus: ukulele show-and-tell friday is a thing 1 bring the terrible playing.
Becca S: also the kitchen has a small resealable box for shared treats (label required). if you want a little poster to advertise "free cookies" i can print one at the front desk. :printer:
Leni Park: printing a poster sounds delightfully extra, yes pls. i'll do a small batch this week and bring them on wednesday. ukulele demo maybe next week if no one throws things. :sweat_smile:
Arlo: welcome Leni! we do an accidental open-mic sometimes at lunch. low-pressure. bring cookies, maybe we'll forgive the ukulele. :laughing:
Omar Z: if you want to store dough overnight, facilities have a small micro-fridge in the lounge with a labeled shelf. ping me and i'll introduce you to them.
Leni Park: perfect. thanks for the warm welcome and all the logistics. excited to join the Growth crew and trade cookie recipes and cringe songs. :sparkles:
